item.title: Dunhuang's creative products draw international visitors at Silk Road expo
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-05
LANZHOU, Nov. 5 (Xinhua) -- At the cultural and creative exhibition area of the 9th Silk Road (Dunhuang) International Cultural Expo, a series of products blending traditional charm with modern design drew visitors' attention. The expo, held from Monday to Wednesday in Dunhuang, northwest China's Gansu Province, brought together around 1,200 representatives from more than 50 countries and regions. It featured forums, cultural exhibitions and artistic performances to showcase Dunhuang's rich culture and promote dialogue on global cultural cooperation. Dillon Thomas Longey, a 20-year-old student from the University of Central Oklahoma in the United States, and his companions moved from booth to booth, admiring Dunhuang-themed products with keen interest. Some bought postcards printed with mural patterns, while others were drawn to plush camels. "This is so cool!" Longey said, describing the integration of history and culture into modern design as a fascinating way to communicate. "Sharing Dunhuang's culture and history through these products is really great!" Because of a tight schedule, Longey only had time to buy a few postcards, but he hoped to choose more cultural products to take back to the United States for family and friends. Briana Corazon Donovan, a 22-year-old American student from the same university, was equally impressed. "Buying a product means you can take culture home with you," she said. These cultural and creative products from northwest China are becoming a window through which foreign visitors can learn about Dunhuang and experience Chinese culture. Dunhuang was once a hub on the Silk Road in northwest China. For centuries, merchants and envoys from different regions passed through, helping create a rich cultural heritage that includes the Mogao Caves. Today, from classic mural figures such as flying apsaras and the nine-colored deer to a wealth of Silk Road elements, ancient Dunhuang culture is being woven into daily life through modern creative design. Sun Xuehu, deputy general manager of Dunhuang Cultural and Tourism Group Co., Ltd., said that in recent years Dunhuang has continued to explore new ways to transform and develop its cultural heritage. Cultural and creative products have expanded from traditional tourist souvenirs into areas such as household goods and artistic design, while cultural consumption options have become increasingly diverse. The Dunhuang Book Center has developed more than 5,000 cultural and creative products. Visitors can read Dunhuang cultural classics while enjoying coffee and browsing products, and can also try their hand at copying murals. At the Dunhuang Press, visitors can make seals and experience woodblock rubbing, gaining a feel for traditional craftsmanship. Data show that in the first half of 2026, Dunhuang received 67,000 overseas visits, up 45.6 percent year on year. As Dunhuang attracts more foreign tourists, its distinctive cultural and creative products are gaining more overseas fans. Shen Hongjie, who runs a woodcarving painting shop in Dunhuang, said his overseas customers often show different interests: some are drawn to desert scenery, others to flying apsara imagery, and still others to relief works. At the same time, more cultural consumption spaces with international elements are appearing in Dunhuang. In the city's Nancang historic and cultural district, a commercial building incorporates images of Silk Road merchants and travelers into its courtyard design. Some restaurants are combining Dunhuang specialty ingredients with Western-style dining, offering creative dishes. Zhang Qi, who is in charge of the project, said that given the growing number of foreign tourists coming to Dunhuang, the project has incorporated international elements into its design and services and employs English-speaking staff. The aim is to provide a more comfortable environment for visitors from different cultural backgrounds to communicate and spend time. From exhibition booths to street-side shops, from traditional art to modern life, Dunhuang culture is reaching visitors from around the world in increasingly diverse ways. Behind these novel products and experiences, what truly resonates is still the appeal of Dunhuang culture itself. Russian scholar Nadezhda Zamyatina, visiting Dunhuang for the first time, is working with a research team from Tianjin University in north China on an urban planning study focused on Dunhuang. During the trip, she bought cultural and creative products such as Dunhuang-themed scarves and teacups. In Zamyatina's view, Dunhuang is an important meeting point of different civilizations, with a rich and unique cultural heritage. She was pleasantly surprised that Dunhuang has not only preserved precious historical heritage but also integrated cultural elements into urban landscapes and daily life, allowing people to touch the city's history in their everyday lives. "Many cities display culture on walls. Dunhuang also uses floor tiles and cultural and creative products to tell its history, which is impressive," Zamyatina said. She found the approach inspiring and hoped other cities would learn from Dunhuang's experience, and that more creative Dunhuang products would appear in the future. For centuries, Dunhuang witnessed encounters and exchanges among different civilizations along the Silk Road. Today, cultural and creative products that foreign visitors pack into their bags will carry Dunhuang's cultural memory across mountains and seas to a wider world. ■

item.title: Canton Fair, CIIE in China highlight shared global gains
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-05
BEIJING, Nov. 5 (Xinhua) -- The ninth edition of the China International Import Expo (CIIE), China's flagship buying platform, opened in Shanghai on Thursday, one day after the 140th Canton Fair, the country's premier export showcase, concluded in Guangzhou. Held back-to-back, the two events offer a fresh lens to examine China's foreign trade. DUAL FAIRS REFLECT CHINA'S TRADE FOOTPRINT The numbers of overseas companies and industry heavyweights attending the 9th CIIE are set to reach record highs this year. More than 300 Fortune Global 500 companies and industry leaders are expected to participate, marking a record high, while over 2,000 companies will be exhibiting for the first time, according to organizers. This year's expo has attracted a record 4,142 overseas exhibitors from 148 countries and regions. In total, 162 countries, regions and international organizations are participating, said China's Ministry of Commerce. On the banks of the Pearl River in south China, a steady stream of orders at the Canton Fair served as evidence of the robust global demand fueling China's export performance. China's total goods imports and exports reached 39.94 trillion yuan (about 5.95 trillion U.S. dollars) in the first three quarters of 2026, with exports at 23.2 trillion yuan, up 16.4 percent year on year, and imports at 16.74 trillion yuan, a 22.3-percent year-on-year increase, according to the General Administration of Customs (GAC). THE STORY BEHIND TRADE FIGURES Trade is not simple arithmetic. Behind the surging trade figures lies a long, interwoven division of labor across global supply chains. A country that is more efficient in a given industry, with more complete supporting capacity and faster delivery, will naturally attract orders. Look beyond the figures, and the fuller picture comes into focus: the surplus is recorded in China, but the gains are shared beyond its borders. The distribution of gains becomes clearer when a product's value chain is laid out. Vehicles built at Tesla's Shanghai plant, many of them shipped directly to Europe and Asia-Pacific markets, are all counted as Chinese exports. This happens every day, as foreign firms operating in China produce for the world. In the first half of 2026, foreign-invested enterprises accounted for nearly 30 percent of China's exports to the European Union, close to 40 percent of exports to the Republic of Korea, and more than 30 percent to emerging markets such as Mexico and Vietnam, according to customs data. Foreign firms contributed 27 percent of China's total exports in 2025, meaning roughly three in every ten goods shipped from China came from a foreign-funded factory. A product labeled "Made in China" may be designed in Germany, use key components from Japan and the Republic of Korea, draw raw materials from Latin America, be assembled in China's Yangtze River Delta or Pearl River Delta, and end up sold in the Middle East, Europe or South America. The product leaves China and the surplus is booked in China's accounts, but the profits are shared along the entire chain. Reading only the surplus without asking how value is distributed yields a partial conclusion. Volkswagen offers a case in point. After more than four decades in China, the group is shifting its strategy from "In China, for China" to "In China, beyond China." "Over recent years, China has developed into a global automotive export hub. Volkswagen Group intends to participate more strongly in this development. We want to scale the capabilities we have built here beyond China," said Ralf Brandstätter, chairman and CEO of Volkswagen Group China. Cars built in China by Volkswagen are already exported to the Middle East and Central Asia, with ASEAN and South America set to follow. The picture looks similar when viewing the aggregate data. In the first three quarters of this year, foreign-invested enterprises recorded 11.69 trillion yuan in imports and exports, up 19 percent year on year and a record high for this period, according to GAC. Trade in intermediate goods rose 27.4 percent to 7.9 trillion yuan, while exports of high-tech products jumped 42.1 percent. More than 150 foreign firms each handled over 10 billion yuan in trade, 20 more than a year earlier, GAC data showed. NEW DEMAND CREATES EXPANDED MARKETS Nor is the market seen as a fixed pie to be divided. Global renewable energy capacity is projected to nearly triple by 2030, a gap that requires vast amounts of clean energy equipment to fill. In the first half of this year, exports by private firms of the "new trio," namely electric vehicles, lithium batteries and photovoltaic products, surged by 45.8 percent. Solar panels, lithium batteries and wind power equipment, meanwhile, are meeting new demand from the global green transition rather than competing for saturated markets. There are more direct examples. Sustained high temperatures have pushed up cooling demand, and Europe's air-conditioning market keeps expanding, with European buyers traveling to Guangzhou to purchase in bulk at the Canton Fair. As more countries accelerate prefabricated construction and tourism camp development, tight housing supply and fast deployment needs inquiries at prefabricated building materials and modular housing booths have also grown rapidly at this fair. A BROADER VIEW OF BALANCED TRADE The surplus also needs to be read alongside the broader balance of payments. China runs a large surplus in goods trade, but deficits in services trade and investment income. Its current account surplus is roughly 3.7 percent of GDP, within the range widely regarded as reasonable internationally. China stands as not only a major seller but also a major buyer. Its imports reached 18.5 trillion yuan in 2025, making it the world's second-largest import market for 17 consecutive years and a major export destination for nearly 80 countries and regions, official data showed. China, notably, does not deliberately pursue a trade surplus and has consistently worked toward more balanced trade. In the first half of 2026, the nation's imports exceeded 10 trillion yuan for the first time in this period. COMPARATIVE ADVANTAGE BEATS ZERO-SUM THINKING The point of economic and trade exchanges is not a zero-sum contest but the use of comparative advantages to deliver development gains to every participant in the chain. Dani Rodrik, a professor at Harvard University, argued in a commentary in August that when major economies are running at near full capacity, trade deficits should not be a cause for concern. Such deficits mean deficit nations consume more goods supplied by surplus economies, a transfer of purchasing power from surplus countries. "Under the current circumstances, then, China's widely criticized surpluses might as well be called enrich-thy-neighbor," he wrote. As the Canton Fair wound down, many buyers headed straight from Guangzhou to Shanghai. Their itineraries show not simply that China is opening up, but that both ends of the supply chain, and partners along it, have something to gain. ■

item.title: 9th China International Import Expo opens in Shanghai
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-05
This photo taken on Nov. 5, 2026 shows a scene during the opening ceremony of the ninth edition of the China International Import Expo (CIIE) and the Hongqiao International Economic Forum in Shanghai, east China. The ninth edition of the CIIE opened on Thursday in Shanghai. (Xinhua/Fang Zhe) SHANGHAI, Nov. 5 (Xinhua) -- The ninth edition of the China International Import Expo (CIIE), the world's first national-level exhibition dedicated to imports, opened on Thursday in Shanghai in east China. Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang delivered a keynote speech at the opening ceremony. Running from Nov. 5 to 10, this year's CIIE has attracted 4,142 overseas exhibitors, including more than 300 Fortune Global 500 companies and industry leaders. Over 480 exhibits are set to make their global, Asian or China debuts at the 2026 event, the highest number in its history. Total exhibition area exceeds 440,000 square meters this year. U.S. exhibitors occupy more than 50,000 square meters, leading for the eighth consecutive year, while companies from Germany, the United Kingdom and France also rank among the top participants. This year's CIIE retains its six major exhibition areas and an innovation incubation section, covering areas such as intelligent industry and information technology, consumer goods, food and agricultural products, automobiles and smart mobility, medical devices and healthcare products, and trade in services. The innovation incubation section features 633 technology and innovation projects from nearly 40 countries and regions, up almost 20 percent from the previous edition. The Hongqiao International Economic Forum, also taking place in Shanghai alongside the CIIE, on Thursday released the World Openness Report 2026, and unveiled its first Export-to-China Capacity Development Report. Announced in 2017 and held annually since 2018, the CIIE serves to give overseas businesses greater access to the vast and growing Chinese market. The past eight editions have drawn more than 180 countries, regions and international organizations and seen over 3,400 new products, technologies and services make their debuts, while cumulative intended deals have exceeded 580 billion U.S. dollars. ■ People visit the France Pavilion during the ninth edition of the China International Import Expo (CIIE) at the National Exhibition and Convention Center (Shanghai) in east China's Shanghai, Nov. 5, 2026. item.title: China open to more U.S. farm imports if reciprocal tariff cuts implemented: commerce spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-05
BEIJING, Nov. 5 (Xinhua) -- China has always been open to expanding its purchases of agricultural products from the United States, but the precondition is that the two sides' arrangement for a 30-billion-U.S. dollar reciprocal tariff reduction is implemented, the Ministry of Commerce said on Thursday. Ministry spokesperson Huang Ling said at a regular press conference that China-U.S. agricultural trade is an important component of bilateral economic and trade cooperation. Expanding agricultural cooperation between the two countries can both enrich the dining tables of the two peoples and provide stable income for businesses and farmers in both countries, bringing tangible benefits to both sides, Huang noted. Huang expressed the hope that the U.S. side can work with China to create more favorable conditions for agricultural trade between the two countries by jointly reducing tariffs, cutting non-tariff barriers and expanding market access. China and the United States held the eighth round of their economic and trade consultations in New York and Washington, D.C. from Sept. 20 to 23. In the consultations, the two sides agreed to reduce tariffs on about 30 billion U.S. dollars worth of goods imported from each other on a reciprocal basis, with tariffs on around 90 percent of the covered products to be lowered to most-favored-nation rates. These reductions will be implemented simultaneously after each side completes domestic legal procedures. ■

item.title: China voices concern over EU's new fees on low-value imports
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-05
BEIJING, Nov. 5 (Xinhua) -- China is highly concerned about the European Union's (EU) new rule of imposing a 2-euro handling fee on low-value imports as of Nov. 1, following a 3-euro customs duty introduced in July this year, the Ministry of Commerce said on Thursday. Ministry spokesperson Huang Ling noted at a regular press conference that cross-border e-commerce, as a new business form and model of international trade, provides diversified choices for global enterprises and consumers. China hopes the EU will assess the impact of relevant policies in a prudent manner and create favorable conditions for China-EU cooperation in e-commerce and other fields, Huang said. ■

item.title: Report highlights China's growing role as global import market
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-05
SHANGHAI, Nov. 5 (Xinhua) -- China is now both a global production hub and a key source of global demand, with a growing capacity to absorb goods from around the world, according to a report released on Thursday in Shanghai in east China. The Export-to-China Capacity Development Report, designed to help other countries boost exports to China, debuted at the ninth Hongqiao International Economic Forum, held as part of the just-opened ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE). As household incomes rise and consumption patterns shift toward higher-quality goods and services, China has considerable room to expand imports of premium products, advanced technologies and services, the report says. China's import mix has evolved from one overwhelmingly dominated by manufactured goods to a more diversified structure encompassing industrial products, energy and raw materials and agricultural commodities, it notes. The report says that China's expanding demand for both high-end manufactured goods and primary commodities offers an inclusive market for economies at different stages of development. The report was jointly compiled by the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences' Institute of World Economics and Politics and the Division on International Trade and Commodities of the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD). It additionally delves into the export performance of 10 of China's trading partners, including Colombia, Kenya, Spain, Thailand and Britain, assessing their potential in the Chinese market and offering recommendations on how to boost exports to China. The World Openness Report 2026 was also released at this forum, warning that global openness is under growing strain amid rising trade protectionism, spreading geopolitical conflicts and profound restructuring of global industrial chains. In 2025, the Global Openness Policy Index stood at 0.7448, down 1.09 percent year on year, while the Openness Performance Index fell 0.9 percent to 0.7458, reversing the recovery seen in both 2023 and 2024, according to the World Openness Report 2026. ■

item.title: World Internet Conference Wuzhen Summit highlights China's open-source AI push
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-04
*Open source has become a defining feature of China's AI development. China's national-level AI open-source communities have attracted over 11 million users, while Chinese open-source large models have been downloaded more than 10 billion times globally. *Experts believe that open source is a key pathway to pooling intelligence and furthering digital inclusion. Practice shows that open source has lowered R&D costs for small and medium-sized enterprises, with particular value for less-used languages and developing countries. HANGZHOU, Nov. 4 (Xinhua) -- At the physical workspace of ModelScope, China's largest AI open-source community, a single developer can do the work of a team. Li Guanghui is among the 249 solo entrepreneurs at this workspace in Hangzhou, capital city of east China's Zhejiang Province, 95 percent of whom are working on AI projects. A former developer at a major tech firm, he relocated to Hangzhou from Guangzhou in south China's Guangdong Province. With AI assistance, he built a hotel-booking mini program entirely on his own, completing in eight months a project that would typically take a team of five to ten people a year to finish. Li's experience reflects a broader trend being discussed at the ongoing 2026 World Internet Conference Wuzhen Summit in Zhejiang's ancient water town of Wuzhen, highlighting how China's open-source push for an inclusive AI future is gaining momentum. The summit has drawn about 1,800 delegates from 138 countries and regions to discuss topics including open source and openness, joint contribution and shared benefits. "ModelScope now serves more than 33 million developers from 239 countries and regions," said Joe Tsai, co-founder and chairman of Alibaba Group, a Chinese tech giant that founded and operates ModelScope. "Through mutual inspiration, they are building a vibrant global ecosystem." Open source has become a defining feature of China's AI development. China's national-level AI open-source communities have attracted over 11 million users, while Chinese open-source large models have been downloaded more than 10 billion times globally. "Open source and openness are the foundation of the internet. Openness generates the massive data that fuels large models," said Ya-Qin Zhang, a foreign academician of the Chinese Academy of Engineering. "Represented by Qwen and DeepSeek, China's open-source efforts are actively contributing to the global ecosystem." Three years ago, Alibaba launched an open-source AI strategy. To date, its Qwen series has released more than 470 open-source models, featuring over 4 billion cumulative downloads and more than 330,000 derivative models worldwide. "AI can only become universal via open source, and only through universality can we create a sustainable and inclusive era of intelligence," said Tsai. He added that Chinese AI companies have converged on open source because it reflects China's innovation spirit: looking beyond self-interest, advancing shared well-being, and creating greater value through mutual achievement. "Why open source? The answer is simple: to bring artificial general intelligence closer, faster," said Gao Xi, a research engineer at China's AI startup DeepSeek. "Those who embrace open source benefit themselves." Experts believe that open source is a key pathway to pooling intelligence and furthering digital inclusion. Practice shows that open source has lowered R&D costs for small and medium-sized enterprises, with particular value for less-used languages and developing countries. In Uganda, a non-profit organization built a local language model based on Qwen's open-source model, covering 68 African languages and helping more Africans break language barriers. Similar efforts using Chinese open-source AI models are emerging across Africa in sectors such as legal services, agriculture, education and insurance. "Based on open-source models, AI is no longer the exclusive domain of a few tech powers, but a cause that all can participate in," Tsai said. "Developers from emerging economies no longer need to start from scratch." John Hoffman, chairman and director of the Global System for Mobile Communications Association (GSMA) Ltd., praised China's push for open technologies. "No openness, no scale; no cooperation, no inclusion," he told Xinhua, adding that openness gave the industry scale, lower costs and a connected world. "Openness is a simple word, but it carries a powerful message about how we develop technology, share knowledge and shape our common future in cyberspace," said Nii Narku Quaynor, chairman of Ghana Dot Com, also known as the "father of the internet in Africa." Open-source AI is, notably, entering public services. China's Mazu intelligent weather early-warning system has been deployed in eight countries, including Pakistan, Ethiopia and Sri Lanka, with cloud trials underway in more than 50 countries as of October 2026. At the Wuzhen summit's exhibition area, a robot powered by Robbyant's LingBot embodied AI models picks up medicines in a simulated pharmacy. This solution, unveiled in July, is already in use at several pharmacies in Shanghai in east China. "China's open source efforts are moving from screens into the physical world," said Zhu Xing, CEO of Robbyant, an embodied AI company under Ant Group, noting that Robbyant's open-source models are increasingly used by overseas researchers as testbeds and starting points for new work. "Pharmacies carry medicines in many forms, bags, boxes, bottles and even transparent packages, placed densely in aisles only around 80 centimeters wide," said Duan Xiaoyue, a market operation specialist at Robbyant. Duan told Xinhua that this puts higher demands on the model's perception and motion planning. In real stores, the system also needs more robust dynamic obstacle avoidance when navigating around elderly customers, wheelchair users, children and pets. The company's LingBot embodied AI models, meanwhile, have been downloaded more than 2.2 million times within nine months, helping lower the entry cost for robotics developers. "Open source is not just about making code visible, but about replacing monopoly with collaboration and breaking boundaries through sharing," said Ni Xingjun, senior vice president of Ant Group and chairman of Ant Group's Technology Strategy Committee. Participants at the summit have also called for broader engagement and responsible development. Quaynor highlighted three dimensions of openness: open documents, open standards and meaningful participation, particularly from Africa and the Global South. Zhang advocated that companies investing in AI should allocate part of their AI budgets to AI governance research and urged jointly developing interoperability standards for AI agents and international safety evaluation platforms to ensure open-source benefits remain controllable and sustainable. "We hope open source can become basic public infrastructure in the digital world, where every participant, regardless of location or seniority, can contribute and benefit on an equal basis," Ni added. (Reporting by Ji Hang, Chen Xiang, Sun Tiexiang, Shang Yiying, Zhang Xuan, Wei Yijun, Zheng Keyi and Yin Xiaosheng; Video reporter: Liu Mingxiang; Video editors: Zhao Xiaoqing, Li Ziwei and Hong Liang.) ■

item.title: Xi Focus: Unlocking a vast market for the world
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-04
SHANGHAI, Nov. 4 (Xinhua) -- After a journey of more than two months across continents and oceans, machinery from WFL Millturn Technologies cleared customs in Shanghai last month for this year's China International Import Expo (CIIE), carrying the Austrian manufacturer's hopes of expanding further into Chinese and wider Asia-Pacific markets. "I don't see any good reason why we will not be successful in China in the upcoming decades," said WFL Managing Director Stefan Hackl. His company will make a double debut: its first appearance at the import expo after more than 20 years in the Chinese market, and the Asian debut of its brand-new machine tool. The company's confidence is rooted in part in the vision behind the CIIE, an initiative championed by Chinese President Xi Jinping, who has personally planned and steered its development. Designed to give overseas businesses greater access to the vast and growing Chinese market, the expo has increasingly turned China's development into opportunities for the world. Now in its ninth year, the CIIE has become a regular fixture on the global trade calendar. Running from Nov. 5 to 10, the expo will bring together 4,142 overseas exhibitors, including more than 2,000 first-time participants like WFL. In the weeks leading up to the expo, shipments from around the world continued to arrive in Shanghai, bringing in a diverse range of products, from Peruvian bananas and French tires to Australian coffee and Kazakh ice cream, all ready to meet buyers at the event. As the world's first national-level exhibition dedicated to imports, the CIIE offers a compelling response to rising protectionism and trade barriers. Rather than viewing trade as a competition for a limited share of global demand, it seeks to make the world economic pie bigger by creating opportunities for businesses and economies to grow together. "Our aim is to turn the China market into a market for the world, a market shared by all, and a market accessible to all," Xi has said. "This way, we will be able to bring more positive energy to the global community." A PROMISE KEPT In his keynote speech at the opening ceremony of the first CIIE in 2018, Xi said the expo is "an important decision made by China to pursue a new round of high-level opening-up, and is China's major initiative to still widen market access to the rest of the world." "China's initiative to expand imports is not a choice of expediency. It is a future-oriented step taken to embrace the world and promote common development," Xi said, pledging that the event would be held annually and "feature good performance, good results and continued success in the years to come." Eight years on, the CIIE has grown into a premier global platform for trade, investment and cultural exchanges, connecting businesses, innovators and consumers from around the world. The promise of an annual expo with lasting results has been borne out by its growth. Past editions have drawn more than 180 countries, regions and international organizations and seen more than 3,400 new products, technologies and services make their debut, while cumulative intended deals have exceeded 580 billion U.S. dollars, according to the organizer. "The CIIE is far more than a trade show," said Jérôme Vanachter, president of Lesaffre Greater China. The French yeast maker is back for a ninth consecutive edition this year. Calling the expo a "market-intelligence hub," Vanachter said the CIIE helps turn market insights into products. Past expos have also seen Xi announce a series of opening-up measures, including advancing the development of pilot free trade zones and the Hainan Free Trade Port (FTP), continuously trimming the negative lists for foreign investment, and expanding the opening of telecommunications, healthcare and other services. These pledges were followed by concrete actions. In November 2024, China removed the last two manufacturing-related restrictions from its national negative list for foreign investment. Last December, the Hainan FTP launched island-wide special customs operations, a milestone in China's drive for high-standard opening-up. "Today, the CIIE has become a showcase of China's new development paradigm, a platform for high-standard opening-up, and a public good for the whole world," Xi said at the fifth edition of the event in 2022. The role of the CIIE in China's opening-up agenda is expected to continue in the years ahead. In its five-year development blueprint for the 2026-2030 period, the country has called for expanding imports and continuing to hold the CIIE and other major trade fairs, including the Canton Fair in south China, while strengthening trade-promotion platforms. A MARKET SHARED BY ALL "Economic globalization represents the trend of history," Xi said at the second CIIE in 2019, likening it to the world's great rivers -- the Yangtze, the Nile, the Amazon and the Danube, which all "surge forward in relentless flow, and nothing can stop their mighty movement." China has been translating this vision into action by opening wider. Quality products from an increasing number of countries are finding a foothold in the Chinese market, generating profits for businesses, wages for workers and tax revenues in their home countries. For 17 consecutive years, China has remained the world's second-largest importer. Also in the first three quarters of 2026, the country's imports rose 22.3 percent year on year, significantly outpacing export growth. "The vastly huge China market is the most promising in the world," Xi noted at the third CIIE in 2020, citing the country's huge population and vast middle-income group. The country's retail sales of consumer goods surpassed 50 trillion yuan (about 7.44 trillion U.S. dollars) for the first time last year, and are expected to grow by another 10 trillion yuan over the next five years. The appeal of the Chinese market is reflected in the growing participation of global businesses in the CIIE, which has attracted a record number of more than 300 Fortune Global 500 companies and industry leaders this year. In terms of exhibition space, U.S. exhibitors lead for the eighth consecutive year, occupying more than 50,000 square meters, while companies from Germany, the United Kingdom and France also rank among the top participants. Over 480 products are set to make their global, Asian or China debut at the event, the highest number in history, underscoring the Chinese market's growing role as a launchpad for global innovation. Under Xi's leadership, China has also sought to make the opportunities offered by its market more accessible to developing countries. For years, the CIIE has provided free exhibition booths to exhibitors from the world's least developed countries. This year, according to the organizer, the exhibition area for African businesses is set to increase steadily, while the space allocated for free booths for the least developed countries will expand by 17 percent. An official delegation from Cote d'Ivoire will make its first appearance at the CIIE's business exhibition this year, showcasing cocoa, coffee, cashews and kola nuts. In May, a zero-tariff policy took effect on imports from all 53 African countries with which China has diplomatic relations. "We are very happy to participate for the first time," said Rami Koné, an official with the country's export agency. "This will be a good opportunity to showcase Cote d'Ivoire to the world." "Of the problems confronting the world economy, none can be resolved by a single country alone," Xi once said. "We must all put the common good of humanity first rather than place one's own interest above the common interest of all." As Xi has pledged, China will continue to open its arms to the world, offering countries greater opportunities for market access, investment and growth. "Together, we can achieve development for all," he has said. ■

item.title: Xi holds talks with Sultan of Oman, stressing bilateral cooperation, peace efforts in Middle East
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
Chinese President Xi Jinping holds talks with Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik Al Said of Oman, who is on a state visit to China, at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 2, 2026. (Xinhua/Li Xiang) BEIJING, Nov. 2 (Xinhua) -- President Xi Jinping said on Monday that China stands ready to work with Oman to steer their strategic partnership to a higher level, and to help restore peace and realize lasting stability in the Middle East at an early date. Xi made the remarks during talks with Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik Al Said of Oman, who is on a state visit to China -- the first by Oman's head of state since the establishment of diplomatic relations between the two countries 48 years ago. The talks constituted an important chapter in the history of China-Oman relations and will inject strong impetus into the development of bilateral ties, Xi said. He said China and Oman should enhance political mutual trust and strengthen exchanges of experience in national governance, while expressing China's support for Oman in safeguarding national independence, sovereignty, security and stability, and in independently exploring a development path suited to its national conditions. The two sides should expand practical cooperation and continuously cement the foundation of mutually beneficial and win-win cooperation, he said, adding that China is committed to promoting high-quality development and expanding high-standard opening up, which will bring greater opportunities to Oman and other countries. China is ready to deepen the synergy of development strategies with Oman and be a stable and reliable partner in the energy sector, a partner with promising potential in investment, and a partner in fostering innovation within advanced technologies, he said. China aims to make bilateral energy cooperation more multi-dimensional and comprehensive, strengthen exchanges in industry, investment, artificial intelligence (AI), science and technology, and people-to-people ties, and join hands on the paths toward development, revitalization, and modernization, Xi said. He also called for efforts to intensify cooperation in such fields as education, tourism, health, media and sports, to continuously substantiate the China-Oman strategic partnership. Xi noted that the Middle East and the Gulf region should not become an arena for major power rivalry or geopolitical conflicts, and that concerted efforts are needed to foster and maintain peace and stability in the region. "China has been actively committed to ending hostilities and promoting peace, aiming to contribute its wisdom and solutions to resolving the regional security predicament," Xi said. China will continue to advocate resolving disputes through political and diplomatic means, and support regional countries in building a common home of good-neighborliness, development, security and cooperation, he added. China is ready to strengthen communication and coordination with Oman and other Arab states and Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries to jointly work for the early restoration of peace and tranquility in the region and the realization of lasting stability, Xi said. Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik said that Oman firmly adheres to the one-China principle and supports China in safeguarding its national sovereignty and territorial integrity. He expressed hope that this visit will serve as a new starting point to explore more cooperation opportunities with China, and build a future-oriented partnership and promote greater development of bilateral relations. Stressing that China has been Oman's largest trading partner for many years and Chinese enterprises' investment in Oman has kept growing, Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik said Oman is ready to synergize development strategies with China and strengthen cooperation in trade, investment, industry, infrastructure, AI, science and technology, and other fields. He said Oman highly appreciates China's just position on the Middle East issue and stands ready to maintain close coordination with China to uphold international law, advocate for the peaceful resolution of disputes, and jointly promote security and stability in the region and beyond. After their talks, the two leaders jointly witnessed the signing of cooperation documents covering areas including industrial and supply chains, green development and digital finance. During the visit, the two sides issued a joint statement on deepening the China-Oman strategic partnership. Prior to the talks, Xi held a welcome ceremony for Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik in the Great Hall of the People. Xi also held a welcome banquet for him at noon. ■ Chinese President Xi Jinping holds talks with Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik Al Said of Oman, who is on a state visit to China, at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 2, 2026.
